transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Friday, November 27. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Watch: Anant Singh 'kicks' driver as he greets crowd from SUV sunroof. A video of Bihar MLA Anant Singh has gone viral, showing him kicking his driver during a wedding. The incident occurred while he was greeting guests at his daughter's wedding, which has drawn significant attention. His daughter's wedding celebrations included elaborate festivities and invitations extended to attendees from across India and Pakistan. Singh emphasized that all guests were welcome, highlighting the importance of community support. Europe's largest technology company SAP is planning to cut 10,000 jobs. SAP SE is reportedly preparing to lay off at least 10,000 employees in a major restructuring initiative. This decision is part of the company's strategy to focus more on artificial intelligence capabilities. The impending job cuts will affect various business units including product, engineering, and sales. Leadership changes within the company also accompany these challenges and the restructuring efforts. Wildlife rebounds on Isle of Wight farmland, with bird numbers nearly tripling. Wildlife recovery has been observed on the Isle of Wight after five years of rewilding efforts. Bird populations at Wilder Little Duxmore nearly tripled, indicating a significant resurgence. Meanwhile, butterfly counts at Wilder Nunwell increased by 117 percent and bumblebee abundance rose by 64 percent . Improvements in soil and water quality were also noted, showing the effectiveness of rewilding processes. Centre turns up heat on Zakir Naik, gives states sweeping powers to enforce IRF ban. The Centre has expanded its crackdown on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation by delegating powers to state governments. This move allows states to freeze funds and restrict property access associated with the IRF. Following a five-year ban extension on the organization, the home ministry issued a notification detailing these powers. Sections 7 and 8 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act now apply on a state level. Yashasvi Jaiswal surpasses Sachin Tendulkar to create history with rare Test feat. Yashasvi Jaiswal has reached an impressive milestone by competing in his 33rd Test match at a different venue, joining the ranks of Sanjay Manjrekar as one of the few players to achieve this feat. Throughout his Test career, he has faced seven distinct teams, with his journey set to advance in the anticipated Border-Gavaskar Trophy against Australia in 2027. Jagan Reddy's YSRCP to back Delimitation Bill in Parliament, but there's a rider. The Jagan Mohan Reddy-led YSRCP will support the NDA government's push for the Delimitation Bill in Parliament, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told news agency ANI on Friday. Surat horror: 6 of Jalgaon family kidnapped, 4 murdered; insurance fraud suspected. An insurance fraud involving two claims may have motivated the kidnapping and murder of a Jalgaon family. Four family members were found dead, while two boys' fates were dramatically different, with one missing and one surviving. The deceased couple was previously accused of fraud related to an insurance claim about a deceased husband. Police are pursuing multiple suspects connected to the kidnapping and ongoing investigation. Court upholds order to move utility pole after years-long neighbour dispute. A Connecticut appeals court has upheld an order requiring neighbours to authorise the removal of a utility pole that has blocked two homeowners from widening their driveway, ending a legal dispute that began in 2019. Watch: Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision, praises Indian teen AI whizz. Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Make in India' initiative during the AI Journey 2026 conference. 17-year-old MP girl stops her child marriage; David Beckham shares her story. Heema Ninama, a determined teenager from Madhya Pradesh, bravely halted her own child marriage with vital support from her principal. Now in Class 12 and aspiring to be a teacher, Heema champions educational access in her community. Her remarkable academic and athletic accomplishments have intrigued international figures like David Beckham. Jensen Huang and wife's foundation gains $2.3B in a day, they have donated $425M. The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO has propelled Lori Huang's foundation to new heights, elevating its value to an impressive $9.7 billion, fueled by significant gains in Nvidia's stock. The foundation's philanthropic endeavors have included noteworthy contributions to institutions like Vanderbilt University, positioning charitable giving as a means for strategic investment in future tech innovations. Despite this success, it maintains a low profile in public awareness.

transcript.title: Money, tax and personal finance
transcript.text: Now to your money — taxes, savings and personal finance. Same fund house, similar stock holdings: These equity mutual fund pairs have 77 percent portfolio overlap; what does it mean?. Beyond this, fund houses have flexibility in deciding how to construct and manage these funds. 8th Pay Commission: Pensioners' body writes to PM Modi, seeks equal benefits for retirees, DA merger; check 11 demands. The scheme aims to upgrade 1.65 lakh post offices, strengthen last-mile delivery and expand e-commerce logistics, with a focus on mail operations, parcel infrastructure and rural connectivity. 8th Pay Commission update: With DA hiked under 7th CPC, what central and state govt employees can expect next. EPFO has urged members to check whether their EPF accounts have become inoperative, a status that can stop interest. Members can claim their balance through the UAN portal with Form 19, or transfer it to a new employer's account with Form 13, after updating their KYC details.

transcript.text: Next, science and technology. It took X 20 years to add parental controls. Can new feature make platform safer for kids?. However, parents cannot read private messages or access their children's search and viewing history. Netflix's coziest show has made a very quiet return. Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China. Harvard's tiny UV light chip could help shrink quantum computers. Harvard-led researchers have developed a microscopic device that generates 120 times more ultraviolet light than previous comparable approaches by efficiently converting red light into UV. The breakthrough could unlock smaller quantum computers, ultra-precise atomic clocks, and compact environmental sensors. AI may put 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk globally over five years: JP Morgan. Artificial intelligence (AI) could displace around 24 million knowledge-worker jobs worldwide over the next five years under an illustrative scenario, as businesses increasingly use the technology to replace tasks currently performed by employees, according to a JP Morgan Wealth Management report. The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year. The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it's one that I've always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks Is Alice Huang a spy or not?. A fat-burning molecule has an unexpected benefit for your muscles. Researchers have discovered that a naturally occurring molecule released during exercise helps muscles become stronger, resist fatigue, and withstand damage. The molecule, already available as a dietary supplement, could open new avenues for treating muscle deterioration associated with type 2 diabetes. Scientists have identified two potentially critical periods when screen time may be especially detrimental to children's learning and memory: infancy and the start of formal schooling. Greater screen exposure during these developmental windows was linked to poorer academic performance and weaker working memory years later. 1Password data breach: How hackers accessed its systems, what data was exposed and are passwords safe?. 1Password disclosed a security breach in which hackers accessed backend systems, exposing customer names, email addresses and account metadata. The company said stored passwords, Secret Keys and encrypted vaults remain safe, with no evidence of account takeovers. Android app developers will soon have to share their address publicly. Independent Android app developers are worried about their privacy after Google announced that from next year many of them will be required to share a phone number and address publicly. The policy change is intended to meet European Union regulations under the Digital Services Act, but Google says contact details will be made public worldwide. Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease. A combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin produced results comparable to antibiotics when used alongside standard treatment for severe gum disease, with benefits persisting long after supplementation ended. The surprising discovery could offer an alternative for some patients while reducing reliance on antibiotics. Vivo X500 series launched in India with 200MP ZEISS camera, 7,800mAh battery: Check price and specifications. Vivo has launched the X500, X500 Pro and X500 Pro Max in India, featuring up to a 200-megapixel ZEISS camera, a Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset and batteries of up to 7,800mAh. Prices start at rupees 1,19,999, with sales beginning on December 3, alongside the launch of the Vivo Watch GT 2 smartwatch. The best Black Friday deals we've already found. This dietary supplement may have an unexpected benefit for the brain. A naturally derived dietary supplement called urolithin A may help the brain get more oxygen and nutrients when it needs them most. In a randomized clinical trial involving 50 middle-aged adults with obesity, researchers found that taking the supplement daily for four weeks increased blood flow to the brain during a challenging memory task, particularly in a region involved in working memory. Nøord has unveiled a $249 keyboard case for Apple's iPhone Duo, featuring a built-in trackpad, five-row keyboard and MagSafe connectivity to create a mini laptop-like setup. Available in Black, White and Titanium, the accessory is expected to start shipping in January 2027. Federal judge blocks the FCC from reviewing ABC's licenses early. Giant horned mammals that emerged shortly after the extinction of the dinosaurs may have had far fewer physical differences between males and females than scientists once believed. transcript.title: Across India
transcript.text: Turning to the big national stories. Centre turns up heat on Zakir Naik: States, UTs get sweeping powers under UAPA to act against banned IRF. The Centre has expanded its crackdown on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation by delegating powers to state governments. This move allows states to freeze funds and restrict property access associated with the IRF. Following a five-year ban extension on the organization, the home ministry issued a notification detailing these powers. Sections 7 and 8 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act now apply on a state level. 'I have endured a lot': Mamata's brother seeks FIR against nephew Abhishek over 'threats'. Mamata Banerjee's younger brother Swapan 'Babun' Banerjee approached Kolkata Police seeking an FIR against nephew and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee, alleging intimidation and obstruction of a blood donation camp. The complaint adds to the family's long-standing feud, which has acquired a political dimension amid Babun's growing proximity to BJP leaders and repeated praise for West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari. Trusts move HC to block chair's casting vote at Tata Sons meet. Tata Trusts have launched a legal challenge against Tata Sons concerning the chairman's casting vote, citing governance issues before a crucial board meeting. They argue that earlier resolutions breach the company's articles and are seeking compensation. Holding a significant stake in Tata Sons, the Trusts aim to ensure their nominee directors' votes carry equal weight, reflecting the continuing tensions over control in India's largest conglomerate. Jagan Mohan Reddy's YSRCP to back NDA's Delimitation Bill push in Parliament but with a rider. The Jagan Mohan Reddy-led YSRCP will support the NDA government's push for the Delimitation Bill in Parliament, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told news agency ANI on Friday. Watch: Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision, praises 16-year-old Indian AI entrepreneur. Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Make in India' initiative during the AI Journey 2026 conference. India playing leading role in global war on terror, says Amit Shah. Amit Shah, the Union home minister, reaffirmed India's unwavering dedication to fighting terrorism while honoring the memories of those affected by the 26/11 attacks. He praised the bravery of both soldiers and innocent civilians, asserting that the Modi government's unwavering stance against terrorism is garnering global recognition. Shah also highlighted that united action is essential, as terrorism remains a grave threat to humanity. Whatever is scarce wins. what you are really selling is trust. Colombo Security Conclave reaffirms commitment to promote regional peace. The Maldives hosted the 8th NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave, uniting member states in their shared goal of enhancing regional peace and security. By emphasizing capacity-building and collaboration, the attendees laid out a roadmap for security cooperation through 2026-27, marking a commitment to address evolving challenges. India reaffirmed its resolve to engage actively with CSC countries to foster stronger ties and collective security measures. Mumbai police issue lookout circulars against CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das. CJP co-convener Saurav Das was barred from flying to London due to a lookout circular. The Centre informed the Delhi high court that this action was taken at Mumbai police's request. Saurav Das's passport is under scrutiny for several discrepancies regarding his identity. His legal team argued that the travel ban infringes upon his fundamental rights. Delhi high court nixes order to cancel NGO's FCRA licence. In a pivotal decision, the Delhi High Court has ruled in favor of the Socio Legal Information Centre, restoring its FCRA licence that was previously annulled by the Home Ministry. The court indicated that there was a lack of evidence to support accusations of the NGO's anti-government actions. Moreover, the court deemed the assertions of the NGO negatively impacting India's image on the global stage as without merit. 'Today one Deepam, tomorrow temples?' Vaishnaw slams TVK govt over Thiruparankundram Deepam row. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the Tamil Nadu government over the Thiruparankundram Karthigai Deepam row, accusing it of hurting the religious sentiments of millions. Judicial member must on bench to confirm PMLA attachment, says Supreme Court. The Supreme Court has ruled that a judicial member must be present in the bench deciding asset attachments. This decision focuses on ensuring legal objectivity in the proceedings related to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The ruling addresses the competence of administrative members in handling questions of law and conflicting judgments. The judgment is applicable prospectively and does not allow reopening of past decisions. 'We love Yogi very much': Sanjay Raut's praise puts spotlight on BJP's biggest UP question. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Thursday seemingly backed Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, describing him as the highest "face of Hindutva" and expressing confidence that he would continue to lead the state after the 2027 state assembly elections. Bihar move illegal, says Supreme Court, quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan. In a significant ruling, the Supreme Court has annulled the Bihar government's controversial decision to release Anand Mohan, who was serving time for murder. The state's attempt to modify prison regulations for his early exit was found unconstitutional. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu criticized the justification threshold for such a change, ultimately mandating that Anand Mohan must surrender within a month. Supreme Court to banks: Give nod to try officials in 7 days. The Supreme Court has demanded that HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital, and PNB Home Finance provide unconditional sanctions. These sanctions involve officials implicated in collusion with builders in housing fraud schemes. The banks' CMDs must articulate their non-compliance in court if not met within a week. CBI's investigations have led to chargesheets, and trials will commence once the necessary sanctions are secured, underscoring the urgency for timely judicial processes. 7 months on, mediation in Sunjay Kapur case hits deadlock. Mediation efforts between Rani Kapur and Priya Sachdev Kapur over Sunjay Kapur's estate ended without resolution. Former Chief Justice DY Chandrachud, who mediated the dispute, reported reaching an impasse. Despite 15 sessions aimed at settlement, both parties did not show flexibility or understanding. The Supreme Court noted that no settlement can be forced upon unwilling parties. Opposition worried, feels government won't risk another defeat. The call for a Parliament session by the BJP to discuss the delimitation bill has taken the opposition by surprise. As uncertainty looms, there are rising concerns among opposition parties about the potential impact on their voting power. The DMK, having previously opposed similar measures, now adopts a cautious stance. In contrast, Congress leaders maintain confidence, even as the government's influence grows.

transcript.title: Around the world
transcript.text: And finally, here is what is happening around the world. New Zealand's ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority by one seat. The right-leaning ruling bloc led by the National Party has fallen short of the majority needed to govern. German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds. Nearly a third of crossings in early 2026 allegedly involved boats or engines from the German man's firm. Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats. Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges. Gérard Depardieu to stand trial for alleged rape of actress in 2018, court rules. A Paris appeals court rules Depardieu will go on trial for the alleged rape of Charlotte Arnould. Pregnant US inmate escapes in prison vehicle after medical appointment. Rebecca Taylor had been imprisoned in New Mexico for multiple theft and burglary charges. Egyptian authorities arrest motorist over tanker crash that killed 31. Officials say the man confessed to travelling at speed and clipping the fuel truck as he was overtaking traffic. Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa. Lenacapavir, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100 percent effective at preventing HIV infection. Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling. A landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) convicted Myanmar of genocide against its Rohingya minority. Tributes for Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor after his death aged 65. Simon Le Bon and his other bandmates say Taylor "brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music". Nine injured, three critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion. Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as officials urged residents to leave the area. Politics and peek-a-boo in Australian parliament as senator brings baby to work. Senator Lidia Thorpe kept 6-month-old Aaliyah entertained, as her mum Senator Fatima Payman, participated in an online safety bill debate. Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza. The killings are the latest from a series of near daily attacks by Israel against what it says are Hamas targets.
